fridge.invention:
A refrigerator equipped with a camera automatically identifies the foods it contains using a computer vision model.
The system estimates, for each food, its opening date and remaining freshness.
Every day it generates recipes that prioritize foods close to their expiry date.
The recipes take into account the allergies and diets of the household.
A smartphone notification warns the user before a product is wasted.

fraud.invention:
Software builds a graph linking the suppliers, bank accounts, addresses and invoices of a company.
A graph neural network detects rings of fake invoices and bank accounts that are shared in a suspicious way.
Each invoice receives a fraud risk score.
The system explains the score by displaying the subgraph of relationships that triggered it.
An analyst validates or rejects the alert, and this feedback retrains the model.

meeting.invention:
An assistant transcribes a video conference meeting in real time and attributes the speech to each participant.
A language model extracts from the transcript the decisions made and the actions to carry out, with their owner and due date.
A participant reviews and validates the list before it is sent.
The validated actions are automatically created in the team's project management tool.
A one page summary is emailed to all participants.
